title: A farther nearby galaxy
hook: Change distance and predict recession speed.
misconception: recession speed stays fixed when distance doubles.
objective: Apply v ≈ H₀d to compare recession speed when distance changes, under the stated assumptions.

claims.text: With the ideal low-redshift linear Hubble relation with fixed Hubble parameter, v ≈ H₀d. When distance doubles, recession speed becomes 2 times its original value.
claims.source: Idealized model v ≈ H₀d; scaling exponent 1. Physics and assumptions await independent review.

recall.question: Consider the ideal low-redshift linear Hubble relation with fixed Hubble parameter, with a nonzero initial result. If distance triples from a positive value, what is the multiplier on recession speed?
recall.why: Apply v ≈ H₀d under the same assumptions: the multiplier is 3.
